corrected_draft.description_long: An SEC Schedule 13D amendment filed by Vivek Ramaswamy and other reporting persons states that he beneficially owned 5,693,897 Strive, Inc. shares, representing 8.4% of the class under the filing’s stated assumption that Class B shares convert to Class A. It explains that Strive’s at-the-market share sales increased the number of outstanding shares, causing the reporting group to fall below the 50% voting-power threshold in its shareholder agreement. The agreement then terminated automatically, and the reporting persons ceased to constitute a group. The amendment says Ramaswamy still beneficially owned more than 5% and would report separately; the other exiting persons fell below 5%. This establishes an ownership disclosure and reporting change. DOJ described the complaint as its latest action against what it called unlawful judicial overreach. corrected_draft.description_short: Vance defends Trump's fake Kharg attack videos as sending Iran a message

corrected_draft.description_long: Reuters reported on August 31, 2026, that Vice President JD Vance defended a social-media post by President Donald Trump showing AI-generated explosions associated with Iran's Kharg Island. Vance characterized the post as a message to Iran rather than an announcement that a military attack had occurred. The timing was notable: Reuters said his explanation came one day after Trump posted the imagery. The supplied account states that the depicted explosions did not represent a real attack on Kharg Island.
